mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES keep drifting below their recent levels, weekday footfall to shopping and dining areas will remain suppressed, so RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks than over the previous four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed below -27% and WORKPLACES below -13% in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain at or below their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week recovery in PARKS after a sharp prior drop signals a substitution back from outdoor recreation toward discretionary indoor spending, which lifts RETAIL_REC within the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 8 points week-on-week after being below -10%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -20.6 to about -11 in the latest two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after PARKS rebounds from below -10% to materially less negative values.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fall together, commuting-linked shopping trips are cut more than either signal alone implies, so the combined downturn depresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series are consistently negative and roughly worsened from t-3w to t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES staying jointly weak or weaker than in the snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in RESIDENTIAL above its already elevated level reflects more time spent at home and fewer discretionary outings, which pushes RETAIL_REC down over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 18% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is persistently positive near 19% across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 18% for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays near flat while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, the pattern is consistent with cautious, necessity-only movement and not broader reopening, so retail-and-recreation demand will stay below the prior four-week average.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -30% while GROCERY_PHARM stays between -2% and +2%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is near zero while TRANSIT is around -33%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean even though TRANSIT remains below -30% and GROCERY_PHARM stays near zero.

mechanism_narrative: A mild upward turn in PARKS after mid-October would usually precede more weekend leisure spending, and that seasonal leisure spillover should raise RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns positive week-on-week from a negative base
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is far less negative now than at t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to outperform its previous four-week average by the end of the next 28 days after PARKS turns up from negative territory.

mechanism_narrative: The retail-recreation series will improve only if mobility restrictions ease enough for transit and workplaces to recover simultaneously; without that coordination, retail demand will remain weak. This means the mechanism is activated only when both series stop falling together.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points and WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series trend weakly and remain below baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES post a same-week recovery of at least the stated size.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains stable while RETAIL_REC is still depressed, households are likely reallocating spending toward essentials rather than discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC should continue to underperform over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is near zero while RETAIL_REC stays around -23% to -25%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day average while GROCERY_PHARM remains near zero and does not show a matching rise.
